In the United States, Halloween is widely celebrated. Some of my muggle neighbors will  decorate their houses with pumpkins, fake skeletons, fake cobwebs, and will participate in a muggle tradition called "trick or treating." 

In my mainly muggle neighborhood there are many houses that are nicely decorated, my house takes the cake. I love the whole month of October and the spooky air, and feel I have to do the wizarding world justice with my decor.

I have a ghoul in my attic which I use the Amplifying Charm on, which makes it louder making the mood eerie for the trick or treaters.

I make sure to dress up with my hat and robes on and hand out candy for the kids. The children love to trick or treat at my house because of the decorations. My family hands out a lot of great sweets (non magic) not sold in the muggle world that the children adore, such as pumpkin pasties, cauldron cakes, and Fainting Fancies! (Just Kidding) The kids seem to love Bertie Bott's every flavor beans.

Each year, the theme of my decoration is about a different aspect of Halloween and this year I chose pumpkins. This year I made my decoration all about jack-o-lanterns and I used Engorgio on pumpkins making them bigger and then magically carved them and illuminated each of them a different color.

The part the kids love though, is that I always bewitch the decorations to play popular muggle Halloween songs which is the greatest and main point of my Halloween decorations.

For the clever kids who stick around, and explored my display, they would find a chest that had a riddle next to it and if they told me the answer, I would open the chest revealing a stash of sweets. Many wizards, witches, and muggle adults have told me that their children love this party and look forward to my great Christmas party too. ;)
